vulnerabilities.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. This vulnerability affects the function sprintf of the file /setup.cgi of the component mini_httpd. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor explains: ""I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know

The Cloud Storage Manager for Fluent Forms – Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, S3 Uploads plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.0. The Shipo plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions 1.6 through 1.8.0. This is due to the `authenticate_rest_user()` function parsing the `LOGGED_IN_COOKIE` value and authenticating the named user without verifying the cookie's cryptographic signature. The function's intended `/wp-json/shipo/` route restriction can also be bypassed by placing that substring in the query string of an unrelated REST endpoint. The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.5. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know or discover an existing campaign and team ID to modify the team's name, story, goal, access and notification settings, set its profile image URL, and upload WordPress-allowed media files as parentless attachments.

The Payment Gateway via Valitor for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 1.9.41 does not properly validate the authenticity of payment callbacks, relying on a verification secret that ships with a hard-coded default value used by every store that has not changed it, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge a valid payment confirmation and mark arbitrary orders as paid.

The MemberDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.7. This is due to a mass-assignment vulnerability in the `user_account_manager()` function's edit_profile branch, where all submitted `$_POST` fields are iterated and directly assigned to the current member object via the `MS_Model` `__set()` magic method with no field allowlist and no capability or ownership check on the submitted `id` parameter. The Burst Statistics  WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not enforce a shared report's date range on the analytics it serves to the report's share link, allowing anyone holding the link to read the report's statistics for any period the site retains rather than the period the report was shared for.

The Multi Step for Contact Form 7 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'multipart field name (array key)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'fv_player_videos' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'buddyforms_form_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable when a form configured with the public_submit option is published — a condition met by the plug

The Auth Armor  WordPress plugin through 1.0.3 does not require authentication on several handlers available to logged-out users, which leak the site's stored API credentials and allow an unauthenticated attacker to reset an administrator's enrollment and take over that administrator account.

The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, which could allow high privilege users such as admin to perform SQL injection attacks.

The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not properly escape a user-supplied value before printing it inside an inline script block on several of its admin screens, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary JavaScript that executes in the session of an administrator who is tricked into opening a crafted link.

The RegistrationMagic  WordPress plugin before 6.1.0.4 does not verify ownership of the submitted email address before updating the associated WordPress user account, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the profile fields of arbitrary non-administrator users by submitting a public form that contains name and primary-email fields.

The Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not perform any authorization or CSRF check before running a schema-altering database maintenance routine, allowing unauthenticated users to convert the Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6's own tables to a narrower character set, which irreversibly replaces every 4-byte character (such as emoji and some CJK characters) in the membership level, discount code and payment records with a question mark.

The Membership Plugin  WordPress plugin before 4.0.6 does not verify that the membership referenced in a saved-card payment request belongs to the user making it, allowing subscriber-level members to disclose another member's Stripe payment client secret and attach a payment method of their choosing to another member's pending payment.

The A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.3 does not properly verify authorization on several of its API command handlers, relying on a signature keyed on a value that is empty by default on an unconnected install, allowing unauthenticated attackers to modify A2Reviews WordPress plugin through 1.2.3 settings and product review metadata and to read non-public product metadata.

The WPGraphQL WordPress plugin before 2.27.1 does not restrict access to posts in custom non-public post statuses, allowing users with the Contributor role and above to read the content of other users' posts in those statuses.

The Burst Statistics  WordPress plugin before 3.7.5 does not check that a reported page view belongs to published content, nor check post status before listing post titles and links in its public statistics output, allowing unauthenticated attackers to disclose the titles and permalinks of draft, pending and private posts.

The Custom Block Builder  WordPress plugin before 3.0.0 does not properly deny unauthorised requests to its REST routes, as its permission checks return a non-error response that WordPress treats as granted, allowing unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary PHP code on the server.
